summary: Feed s157_double to IDS is degraded: 12.4% duplicate packets and severe tool overload (3.02 Gbps bursts vs 1 Gbps port, 302% capacity) risking drops and missed detections.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is sending bursty aggregated traffic (peak 3.02 Gbps in 1ms intervals) to a single 1 Gbps IDS port without load balancing or rate shaping. Three intervals exceeded 80% capacity threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC buffers overflow and drops packets during bursts, causing incomplete flow reassembly, missed signatures, and blind spots for detection. IDS cannot inspect full payload at line rate.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across multiple 1 Gbps IDS ports/instances with 5-tuple hashing to keep per-port utilization <70% and preserve flow coherence for IDS stateful inspection

findings.root_cause: Same packets delivered via two SPAN/mirror paths or packet broker aggregation without deduplication - 230 of 1851 packets (12.4%) are exact duplicates, exceeding 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU/capacity processing duplicates, inflates connection counts and alerts, distorts analytics, and exacerbates the existing 3x overload, increasing chance of missing real attacks.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop identical packets within a short window before load balancing to IDS, freeing ~12% capacity and ensuring clean single-copy feed
